{r}

#| include: false

# get data and load standard data processing
source("transit_data_processing.R")  

hts_source <- "Puget Sound Regional Council (PSRC) 2017-2025 Household Travel Survey"


{r palettes, include=FALSE}
psrc_fill_dec <- list(
  Transit = psrc_colors$purples_dec[1:5],
  rgcs = psrc_colors$oranges_dec[1:5],
  survey_year = psrc_colors$blues_dec[1:5],
  mode_class_5 = psrc_colors$greens_dec[1:5]
  )

psrc_fill_segment <- list(
  income_binary = c("#91268F", "#8CC63E"),
  income = psrc_colors$pgnobgy_5,
  gender = c("#F05A28", "#00A7A0", "#91268F", "#8CC63E"),
  race_binary = c("#91268F", "#00A7A0"),
  race_ethnicity = psrc_colors$pognbgy_10,
  age = psrc_colors$gnbopgy_5,
  home_county = psrc_colors$obgnpgy_10,
  in_rgc = c("#00A7A0", "#8CC63E"),
  res_type_group = c("#91268F", "#F05A28")
  )

Overview

The Household Travel Survey asks various questions about transit use and transit access. This information can then be paired with other information including if someone lives in a regional growth center.

Total trips

Total trips in the region have exceeded pre-pandemic numbers.

Walk trips peaked in 2021.

{r}
#| label: fig-total-trips
#| fig-cap: Total Trips in Region
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 4.5

hts_data_mode <- hts_bin_mode(hts_data)

df <- psrc_hts_stat(hts_data_mode, "trip", "mode_class_5", incl_na=FALSE) 

df$mode_class_5 <- factor(df$mode_class_5,
                          levels = c("Bike/Micromobility", "Drive", "Other",
                                     "Transit", "Walk"))

df_count <- psrc_hts_stat(hts_data_mode, "trip", "mode_class_5", incl_na=FALSE) %>% group_by(survey_year) %>% summarise(total = sum(est))

df_count$tot_rounded <- round(df_count$total, digits = -2)

ggplot(df_count, 
       aes(x = factor(survey_year), y = total)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = factor(survey_year)), 
               width = 0.7
           ) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(total, -2)),
                vjust = -0.3
            ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#cbcbcb", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = psrc_fill_dec[["survey_year"]]) + 
  psrc_style() + 
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title = element_blank())
    
    # function sourced from Analysis/util.R
    get_table_format(df)



{r}
#| label: fig-total-trips
#| fig-cap: Total Trips in Region
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 4.5

hts_data_mode <- hts_bin_mode(hts_data)

df <- psrc_hts_stat(hts_data_mode, "trip", "mode_class_5", incl_na=FALSE) 

df$mode_class_5 <- factor(df$mode_class_5,
                          levels = c("Bike/Micromobility", "Drive", "Other",
                                     "Transit", "Walk"))

df_count <- psrc_hts_stat(hts_data_mode, "trip", "mode_class_5", incl_na=FALSE) %>% group_by(survey_year) %>% summarise(total = sum(est)) %>%
  mutate(est_rounded = total/1000000)

# df_count$tot_rounded <- round(df_count$total, digits = -2)

ggplot(df_count, 
       aes(x = factor(survey_year), y = est_rounded)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = factor(survey_year)), 
               width = 0.7
           ) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(est_rounded, 1)),
                vjust = -0.3
            ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#cbcbcb", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = psrc_fill_dec[["survey_year"]]) + 
  psrc_style() + 
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title = element_blank())



{r}
#| label: fig-share-trips
#| fig-cap: Share of Trips in Region
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 10

ggplot(filter(df, !is.na(mode_class_5)),
       aes(x=factor(survey_year), y=prop, fill=factor(survey_year))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label=scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 1)),
                vjust = -0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#cbcbcb", linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ mode_class_5, ncol=5)+
  scale_fill_manual(values = psrc_fill_dec[["mode_class_5"]])+
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, 
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  psrc_style() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", # remove legend
        strip.text = element_text(size = 10.5), # adjust text size on facet title (variable values)
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(0.5, "lines"), # add spacing between facet grids
        axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10.5), # adjust text size for axis text (years)
        axis.text.y = element_blank())

Transit trips

Transit trips have continued to increase post-pandemic, but have not reached pre-pandemic levels.

In 2025, there was a significant increase in transit trips by count and share compared to 2021 and 2023.

{r}
#| label: fig-transit-trips
#| fig-cap: Transit Trips in Region
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| fig-width: 3
#| 
## transit trips count
df2 <- df %>% filter(mode_class_5=="Transit") 
df2$est_rounded <- round(df2$est, digits = -2)

transit_count <- ggplot(df2, 
       aes(x = factor(survey_year), y = est_rounded)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = factor(survey_year)), 
               width = 0.7
           ) +
  # geom_text(aes(label = round(est_rounded, 1)),
  #               vjust = -0.3
  #           ) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::number(round(est/100000, 1), accuracy = 0.1, big.mark = ",")), size = 8,
                vjust = -0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#cbcbcb", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = psrc_fill_dec[["Transit"]]) + 
  psrc_style() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", # remove legend
        trip.text = element_text(size = 16), # adjust text size on facet titsle (variable values)
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(0.5, "lines"), # add spacing between facet grids
        axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20), # adjust text size for axis text (years)
        axis.text.y = element_blank())

Transit frequency

In 2025, there was a significant increase in transit use 2-4 days a week.

In 2025, there was a significant increase in transit use 1-3 days a week.

Transit frequency of 5 days a week has not returned to pre-pandemic levels.

In 2025, there was a significant decrease in the share of riders that answered they never in the past 30 days used transit. Historically, 75% to 84% of respondents said they have not used transit in the past 30 days. That dropped to 67% in 2025.

{r}
#| label: fig-transit-freq-share
#| fig-cap: Transit Frequency in Region
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 10
#|

df5 <- psrc_hts_stat(hts_data, "trip", c("transit_freq_bucket"), incl_na=TRUE)

df5$transit_freq_bucket <-
  factor(df5$transit_freq_bucket,
         levels = c("6-7 days a week", "5 days a week", "2-4 days a week", "1 day a week", "1-3 days in the past month", 
        "Never in the past 30 days"))

ggplot(df5,
       aes(x=transit_freq_bucket, y=prop, fill=factor(survey_year))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label=scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 1)),
                vjust = -0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#cbcbcb", linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ survey_year, ncol=5)+
  scale_fill_manual(values = psrc_fill_dec[["survey_year"]])+
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, 
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  psrc_style() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", # remove legend
        strip.text = element_text(size = 10.5), # adjust text size on facet title (variable values)
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(0.5, "lines"), # add spacing between facet grids
        axis.title = element_blank(),
       axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10.5, angle = 45, hjust = 1), # adjust text size for axis text (years)
        axis.text.y = element_blank())


{r}

                                  title='Transit Use Frequency',
                                  moe='prop_moe'
) + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(size=14),

        axis.title.y=element_text(size=20),

Access to transit trips

Walked or jogged is by far the most dominant way people access transit.

The share of walked or jogged has significantly increased in 2023 and 2025 compared to 2019 and 2021. Accessing transit by vehicle has significantly decreased over the same time period.

Transit use by income

In 2025, members of households with an income under $50,000 are significantly more likely to use transit compared to people in other income brackets.

In 2025, there was a significant increase from 2021 and 2023 in share of people in households with an income of $50,000 to $99,999 and $100,000 or more using transit. 2025 was comparable to pre-pandemic transit use by people in these two income brackets.

{r}
#| label: fig-transit-income-share
#| fig-cap: Transit Ridership by Income in Region - 2025
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| fig-width: 3
#|
df8 <- psrc_hts_stat(hts_data_mode, "trip", c("income_3group", "mode_class_5"), incl_na=FALSE) %>%
  filter(mode_class_5=="Transit") %>% 
  filter(survey_year=="2025") %>%
  filter(income_3group!="Prefer not to answer")
df8$est_rounded <- round(df8$est, digits = -2)

transit_income_share <- ggplot(df8, aes(x=factor(income_3group), y=prop, fill=factor(income_3group))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label=scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 1)),
                vjust = -0.3, size = 8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#cbcbcb", linewidth = 0.3) +
  #facet_wrap(~ mode_class_5, ncol=5)+
  scale_fill_manual(values = psrc_fill_segment[["income"]])+
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent,

df12.2

Transit/mode share by disability status

The question about disability status was added to the Household Travel Survey in 2023.

People who do not have a disability increased their share of transit ridership from 2.4% to 3.7% from 2023 to 2025. This was a significant increase.

People with a disability use of the Other mode share jumped significantly from 2023 to 2025 from 1.6% to 7%. The Other mode includes paratransit and ride hail services such as Uber/Lyft, taxi, or car service.

Driving is the dominant mode for people with a disability.

Transit trips and trip miles

Due to lower counts for higher mile trips, limit takeaways to looking at zero to six miles and six to 12 miles compared to everything else.

There are meaningful trends to take away in general.

In 2023, when transit is the primary mode there was a decrease in length of trips from zero to six miles and increase of trips six to 12 miles.

Other than in 2023, when transit is the primary mode over 50% of transit trips are zero to six miles.

{r}
#| echo: false

df21 <- psrc_hts_stat(hts_data_mode, "trip", c("mode_class_5", "distance_miles"), incl_na=FALSE) %>% filter(mode_class_5=="Transit") %>% #filter(survey_year=="2025") %>% 
  filter(distance_miles!='Exactly 0') %>% filter(distance_miles!='Missing')

transit_miles_chart <- static_column_chart(df21, x='distance_miles', y='prop', fill='survey_year',ylabel= 'Share', xlabel='Miles', title='Trip Length when Transit is Primary Mode - Share', moe='prop_moe', color='pgnobgy_10' ) + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(size=14), axis.text.y=element_text(size=14), legend.text = element_text(size=14), axis.title.y=element_text(size=20), axis.title.x=element_text(size=20))

transit_miles_chart

Trip miles by regional growth centers

People who live in a regional growth center take shorter trips (all modes) from zero to six miles compared to those who live outside of regional growth centers.

{r}
#| echo: false

  filter(distance_miles!='Exactly 0') %>% filter(distance_miles!='Missing')

rgc_miles_chart <- static_column_chart(df21.4, x='distance_miles', y='prop', fill='rgchome',ylabel= 'Share', xlabel='Miles', title='Distance in Miles per Trip by RGC - Share', moe='prop_moe', color='pgnobgy_10' ) + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(size=14), axis.text.y=element_text(size=14), legend.text = element_text(size=14), axis.title.y=element_text(size=20), axis.title.x=element_text(size=20)) + facet_wrap(~ survey_year)

df21.4

Vehicle ownership and regional growth centers

People who live in a regional growth center are significantly more likely to live in a household without a vehicle.

{r}
#| label: fig-vehicle-ownership-home-rgc
#| fig-cap: Vehicle Ownership by Home RGC 
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 6
#| 

# no vehicle ownership by rgc
df22 <- psrc_hts_stat(hts_data, "hh", c("rgchome", "vehicles"), incl_na=FALSE) 

veh_rgchome <- ggplot(df22, aes(x=factor(vehicles), y=prop, fill=factor(rgchome))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label=scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 1)),
                vjust = -0.3, size = 8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#cbcbcb", linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ survey_year, ncol=5)+
  scale_fill_manual(values = psrc_fill_dec[["survey_year"]])+
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, 
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  psrc_style() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", # remove legend
        trip.text = element_text(size = 16), # adjust text size on facet titsle (variable values)
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(0.5, "lines"), # add spacing between facet grids
        axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 16), # adjust text size for axis text (years)
        axis.text.y = element_blank())

df23

Number of vehicles and transit riders

During the pandemic in 2021, 61% of transit riders live in a zero vehicle household.

In 2023, transit riders living in a household with one vehicle came back to riding transit and ridership was comparable to riders living in zero vehicle households.

In 2025, transit riders living in a household with two vehicles came back to riding transit comparable to riders living in zero or one vehicle households.

{r}
#| echo: false

        color='pgnobgy_10' ) + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(size=14), axis.text.y=element_text(size=14), legend.text = element_text(size=14), axis.title.y=element_text(size=20), axis.title.x=element_text(size=20))
